Use case: style-transfer / architectural interior design study. Create one polished landscape cabin DESIGN REVIEW BOARD for a Star Trek tabletop map project. Show two large true orthographic directly-overhead room views side by side, no perspective or isometric tilt, ceilings removed. Left: STANDARD QUARTERS. Right: OFFICER QUARTERS. Use the SAME physical scale in both panels: standard room 7.5 m square; officer room 9 × 9 m outer envelope with a 3 × 3 m square missing from its upper-right corner. Keep the officer footprint a genuine L, not a square with something inserted into its corner. Add a thin neutral dark background around the rooms. This is one review board, not a sprite sheet for automatic cutting.
Reference image 1 is the existing STANDARD ROOM GEOMETRY and furniture positions. Reference image 2 is the existing OFFICER ROOM GEOMETRY and furniture positions. Reference image 3 supplies the approved CORRIDOR MATERIAL STYLE ONLY; do not borrow its corridor/alcove shape.
Preserve existing room topology and furniture locations. Standard: open main entrance centered on bottom wall; short hull window in top wall left of bathroom; bed upper-left, desk/chair down the left, sofa/table lower-right. Bathroom in upper-right attached to top and right perimeter walls, open doorway in its left partition; basin, toilet, sonic shower, no bathtub. Officer: entrance centered on bottom wall, hull window on top wall to right of bathroom, bed against right wall below missing corner, desk/chair lower-left, sofa/table lower-right. Larger bathroom upper-left against top and left perimeter walls, doorway in its right partition; basin, toilet, a separate sonic shower and a bathtub. The bathroom must not become an island room inside the room. Keep bathroom standing areas and main walking routes open. No additional walls, doors, furniture islands or windows.
Re-style built-in furniture and wall finishes so these read as Starfleet living quarters rather than a modern hotel or generic sci-fi room. Include restrained wall-panel seams, subtle illuminated trim, integrated LCARS desk displays and fitted storage fronts within the wall bands. Beds retain single-person proportions; do not enlarge furniture. Sonic showers use flush control/emitter panels, not contemporary shower heads. Windows stay in their current hull-wall locations, no exterior scene.
No door leaves across any opening: native game doors will be separate. No people, no huge ceiling arches occluding the floor, no decorative clutter, no saturated neon, no labels inside the floor plan. Small exact labels above views: "STANDARD QUARTERS", "OFFICER QUARTERS". Room images should show realistic, softly lit pre-rendered materials with thin readable wall tops. Geometry must remain recognizable from the source images.
Style: GALAXY CLASS, matched to reference image 3: warm taupe/ivory curved built-in panels, soft rounded furniture edges, muted mauve carpet with restrained warm border bands, understated dark wood-toned desk or shelf accents, warm neutral indirect lighting, plum/slate upholstered seating and coordinated bedding, amber/lavender LCARS. Comfortable Enterprise-D-era domestic atmosphere. Bathrooms use warm ivory molded fixtures and understated pale non-slip flooring. Avoid cooler industrial Voyager ribs here. Exact board heading: "GALAXY-CLASS QUARTERS".
